newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Feb 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Feb 6.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:

* The Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter merger fuels speculation about mergers involving other prominent firms such as Lehman Bros, PaineWebber, Salomon Bros and the Equitable Cos' Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette unit.
* The Dow industrials fell as much as 122 points from Tuesday's close before ending down 86.58 points at 6,746.90, led by steep declines in technology stocks.
* U.S. Vice President Al Gore says the Clinton Administration will try to impose new public interest programming obligations on broadcasters once they begin high-definition digital television.
* Apple Computer Chief Executive Gilbert Amelio offers no new initiatives in his speech to shareholders, but draws applause by promising to attack the competition with tougher marketing efforts.
* The Federal Reserve decides to leave interest rates unchanged, continuing a yearlong pattern in which it has kept monetary policy on hold.
* Bond traders ignored the Fed's decision, and the yield on the 30-year bond rose to 6.75 percent from 6.70 percent.
* Switzerland's three largest banks have decided to create a fund with an initial worth of about $70 million for Holocaust victims.
* Roche Holding said it has agreed to buy Tastemaker flavor business from two U.S. companies, Mallinckrodt Inc and Hercules Inc, in a deal valued at about $1.1 billion including assumption of debt.
* Goodyear Tire & Rubber ended its partnership with Bridgestone Corp, forming an alliance instead with Sumitomo Rubber, and took an $872.5 million write-down against the fourth quarter.
* Mattel's fourth quarter net income rose 1.3 percent to $0.41 per share; its earnings before charges rose 22 percent.
* Sony raises its profit forecast for the full fiscal year by 26 percent after posting earnings that doubled in the fiscal third quarter.
* U.S. Robotics has begun television advertising to attract a broader spectrum of Internet users.
* Manufacturing, nonprofit, financial and government groups have formed an organization to try to keep manufacturing jobs in New York City.
* The dollar rose past 123 yen for the first time in four years but ends mostly lower against other currencies.
* Copper futures rose to their highest prices in eight months on reports pointing to strong demand.
